title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
benchmark_measurement: Qualitative analysis of user experiences where LLM recommendations (e.g., Western-style meditation or therapy) conflicted with their religious or cultural practices (e.g., prayer). This was not a formal benchmark but an observation from user interviews.
religious_groups: General religious practices (e.g., prayer, meditation as prayer)
findings: General-purpose LLMs demonstrated cultural misalignment by providing mental health recommendations that favored Western, secular approaches (e.g., 'go to therapists'). These suggestions were sometimes inappropriate for users from different cultural and religious backgrounds, for whom practices like prayer would have been a more suitable and familiar form of support.
